# Object Decomposition and Composition


## Overview
Object Decomposition and Composition refers to a family of NeRF architectures that explicitly separate a scene into distinct semantic or geometric entities (objects) to enable instance-level editing, manipulation, and analysis [G]. Unlike standard NeRFs that treat the scene as a monolithic volume, these methods introduce mechanisms to identify, isolate, and recombine individual objects [G]. This family is distinguished from siblings like [Signed Distance Function (SDF) Representations](12495-signed-distance-function-sdf-representations.md) by its focus on semantic/instance separation rather than just boundary representation, and from [Mixture-of-Experts and Modular Architectures](14429-mixture-of-experts-and-modular-architectures.md) by its specific goal of compositional scene editing rather than just computational efficiency [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Model Architecture Modifications](11313-model-architecture-modifications.md).

## Subtopics

### [DM-NeRF](13525-dm-nerf.md)
Simultaneously reconstructs continuous 3D scene geometry, decomposes all individual objects in 3D space, and supports flexible object shape manipulation from 2D images only. Sets it apart by introducing an explicit object field that predicts a one-hot object code for every 3D point, enabling instance-level editing without explicit mesh extraction. Choose when instance-level editing without mesh extraction is required.

### [Unified Decompositional and Compositional NeRF](14413-unified-decompositional-and-compositional-nerf.md)
Two-stage framework that jointly learns object-level and scene-level implicit representations to enable both novel view synthesis and instance-level scene editing. Sets it apart by uniting decomposition and composition in a single pipeline where a coarse global field guides sampling for a fine-grained decomposed field, re-composed using differentiable one-hot activation weights. Choose when joint learning of object and scene representations is required.

### [Detail-based Segmentation](15935-detail-based-segmentation.md)
Divide-and-conquer strategy for representing complex scenes using multiple NeRFs by partitioning objects based on their detail frequency. Sets it apart by relying on a frequency threshold derived from object detection masks to determine segmentation, assigning high-frequency objects to individual NeRFs and low-frequency ones to a joint NeRF. Choose when rendering quality for detailed regions needs improvement by reducing the learning burden on each network.

### [Neural Articulated Radiance Field (NARF)](18597-neural-articulated-radiance-field-narf.md)
Models articulated objects by decomposing them into rigid parts, each represented by a separate Rigidly Transformed Neural Radiance Field (RT-NeRF). Sets it apart by explicitly estimating rigid transformations via forward kinematics to ensure each part maintains a consistent radiance field across different 3D pose configurations, avoiding part dependency issues. Choose when modeling articulated or deformable objects with known kinematics is required.

### [Fig-NeRF](12006-fig-nerf.md)
Scene composition model for object interpolation and amodal segmentation using two separate NeRF models for foreground and background. Sets it apart by employing a deformable model for the foreground and a latent-conditioned appearance model for the background, enabling explicit manipulation of object shape and appearance. Choose when amodal segmentation and object interpolation are required.

#### Dual-Payway NeRF
- [S1] A division of NeRF into a dual-pathway architecture comprising a scene (background) branch for encoding scene geometry/appearance and an object (foreground) branch for individual object encoding.
- [S1] Eliminates the need for separate training per object by assigning activation codes to training rays for each object.
- [S1] Renders transformed objects using the conditioned object branch and the background from the scene branch together, with an object manipulator for precise radiance and object field editing that accounts for collisions and occlusions.

#### CompoNeRF / Set-the-Scene
- [S1] Methods that address guidance collapse in scene-level editing by representing scenes as compositions of multiple locally optimized NeRFs integrated globally.
- [S1] Decompose and reassemble scenes through proxy manipulation for editing without additional fine-tuning, adjusting text guidance levels to ensure entity distinctiveness while maintaining scene coherence.

## Background
Subsequent research has led to the division of NeRF into a dual-pathway architecture comprising a scene branch for encoding geometry/appearance and an object branch for individual encoding [S1]. These models learn to encode multiple objects simultaneously by assigning activation codes to training rays, eliminating separate training per object [S1]. For view generation with manipulation, they render transformed objects using the conditioned object branch alongside the background, with an object manipulator handling collisions and occlusions [S1]. CompoNeRF and Set-the-Scene address guidance collapse in scene-level editing by representing scenes as compositions of multiple locally optimized NeRFs integrated globally [S1]. Through proxy manipulation, scenes can be decomposed and reassembled for editing without additional fine-tuning [S1].
